note: Reviewed plain-language descriptions of what common blood tests measure. Descriptive only: no diagnostic or treatment statements.

entries.definition: Hemoglobin is the protein inside red blood cells that carries oxygen. This test measures how much hemoglobin is in the blood.
Hematocrit measures the proportion of the blood that is made up of red blood cells, expressed as a percentage.
White blood cells are part of the immune system. This test counts how many white blood cells are in a given volume of blood.
Red blood cells carry oxygen from the lungs to the rest of the body. This test counts how many red blood cells are in a given volume of blood.
Platelets are small cell fragments that help blood clot. This test counts how many platelets are in a given volume of blood.
MCV measures the average size of the red blood cells.
MCH measures the average amount of hemoglobin inside each red blood cell.
MCHC measures the average concentration of hemoglobin within the red blood cells.
RDW measures how much the red blood cells vary in size from one another.
Neutrophils are the most common type of white blood cell. This test reports how many neutrophils are present, as a count or as a percentage of all white blood cells.
Lymphocytes are a type of white blood cell. This test reports how many lymphocytes are present, as a count or as a percentage of all white blood cells.
Monocytes are a type of white blood cell. This test reports how many monocytes are present, as a count or as a percentage of all white blood cells.
Eosinophils are a type of white blood cell. This test reports how many eosinophils are present, as a count or as a percentage of all white blood cells.
Basophils are the least common type of white blood cell. This test reports how many basophils are present, as a count or as a percentage of all white blood cells.
Glucose is the main sugar the body uses for energy. This test measures the amount of glucose in the blood at the time the sample was taken.
HbA1c reflects the average blood glucose level over roughly the previous two to three months, by measuring how much glucose has attached to hemoglobin.
Creatinine is a waste product from normal muscle activity that the kidneys filter out of the blood. This test measures its level in the blood.
eGFR is a calculated estimate of how much blood the kidneys filter per minute, derived from the creatinine result together with other factors.
Urea is a waste product formed when the body breaks down protein; the kidneys remove it from the blood. This test measures its level in the blood.
Sodium is an electrolyte that helps regulate the body's fluid balance, nerves, and muscles. This test measures its concentration in the blood.
Potassium is an electrolyte important for nerve and muscle function, including the heart. This test measures its concentration in the blood.
Chloride is an electrolyte that works with sodium and other electrolytes to maintain fluid and acid-base balance. This test measures its concentration in the blood.
Calcium is a mineral involved in bones, muscles, nerves, and blood clotting. This test measures the amount of calcium in the blood, which is separate from the amount stored in bone.
ALT is an enzyme found mostly in the liver. This test measures the amount of ALT in the blood.
AST is an enzyme found in the liver and several other tissues, including muscle. This test measures the amount of AST in the blood.
ALP is an enzyme found mainly in the liver and bones. This test measures the amount of ALP in the blood.
GGT is an enzyme found mainly in the liver. This test measures the amount of GGT in the blood.
Bilirubin is a yellow substance produced when red blood cells break down; the liver processes it. This test measures its level in the blood.
Albumin is the most abundant protein in blood plasma, made by the liver. It helps keep fluid in the bloodstream and carries various substances.
This test measures the combined amount of all proteins in the blood, mainly albumin and globulins.
Cholesterol is a fatty substance used to build cells and certain hormones. This test measures the total amount of cholesterol carried in the blood.
LDL is one of the particles that carries cholesterol in the blood, often described in reports as a target for monitoring. This test measures the cholesterol carried by LDL particles.
HDL is one of the particles that carries cholesterol in the blood. This test measures the cholesterol carried by HDL particles.
Triglycerides are a type of fat the body uses to store and transport energy. This test measures their level in the blood.
TSH is a hormone from the pituitary gland that signals the thyroid gland to produce thyroid hormones. This test measures the TSH level in the blood.
Ferritin is a protein that stores iron. Its blood level is commonly used as an indicator of the body's iron stores.
CRP is a protein made by the liver whose level rises with inflammation in the body. This test measures the CRP level in the blood.
This test measures the storage form of vitamin D in the blood. Vitamin D is involved in calcium absorption and bone health.
Vitamin B12 is needed to make red blood cells and to keep nerves working. This test measures its level in the blood.
This test measures the amount of iron circulating in the blood at the time of the sample. Iron is needed to make hemoglobin.
